solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stick tiny quantity of water on sweet

parts.note: to stick something is to gum it
a drop is a tiny amount of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone dabs a little water on a sweet to make something stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy jelly confection, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Good girl in northwest Spain

parts.note: Alicia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl is living in northwestern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Galicia is the autonomous region occupying the northwest corner of Spain.

clue.text: Large amount of motivational research first for head of criminal organisation

indicators.note: first says that the research abbreviation leads, ahead of the size word

parts.note: MR is an abbreviation for motivational research
big means large

explanation.surface: A lot of motivational research is the first priority for a boss of a crime syndicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amount of' is a link joining Large to its partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Big is the slang name for the leader of a gang or criminal network.

clue.text: Song or two about the Orient

indicators.note: the two songs sit around the next piece

parts.note: two songs: a round, sung in canon by several voices, and a lay, an old narrative poem or ballad
the second of the two songs
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A singer offers a tune or two about the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song or two' reads as one song or a few, but 'Song' is the definition and 'two' supplies two more songs which sit 'about' the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a refrain, often a dance song.

clue.text: Group of animals coming before the fall?

definitions.meaning: a family of lions is collectively called by this word
the proverb says that self-satisfaction goes before a fall

explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for lions, and the vanity that the proverb says comes before a fall.

clue.text: Right away hit song was remixed

indicators.note: a remixed track has its parts rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A chart hit was given a new mix straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on sight means immediately, the moment it is seen, so right away.

clue.text: Undressed?

parts.note: gear is slang for clothes, so someone without clothes is jokingly said to have none on, like a car in neutral

explanation.definitionFit: A car out of gear is in neutral; read playfully, gear is clothing, so the phrase means unclothed.

clue.text: Tree French novelist climbed

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French novelist, author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A French writer scaled a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree with red fruit clusters.

clue.text: You reportedly found in entrance Alma reconstructed in the country

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the entrance word

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as heard rather than written

parts.note: the word you said out loud is the letter U

indicators.note: reconstructed means rebuilt, so these four letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: You'll find, they say, a woman called Alma rebuilt in an entrance somewhere in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You reportedly' is a sound-alike convention: the pronoun heard aloud is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a country in Central America.

clue.text: Take a risk for fashion?

definitions.meaning: to chance one's luck cheekily, seeing what one can get away with
to put on a garment in a shop to see whether it suits

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means attempting something cheeky to see if it works, and putting clothes on to test the fit.

clue.text: Liberal about to include gentleman retiring as workers' champion

indicators.note: the word about is made to hold the next piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so this title is read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a gentleman or knight

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician absorbs a modest gentleman and becomes a champion of the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' champion' points to the British Labour movement, the party of organised workers, rather than any general advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labourist is a supporter of the Labour movement, hence a champion of working people.

clue.text: Full of subject-matter or beef perhaps

definitions.meaning: a substantial piece of writing with plenty of content is described this way
beef is an example of a food that consists of flesh, like steak or lamb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both substantial in content and consisting of animal flesh, beef being one such food.

clue.text: Many grew old behind bars

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword convention for many
to have aged is to have grown old

explanation.surface: Lots of people grew old while in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept behind bars is confined in an enclosure, as a bird in a cage.

clue.text: About fifteen in charge included are competent

indicators.note: about can mean around or astir, signalling that the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A group of about fifteen people in charge are said to be competent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' is a link word saying the in-charge abbreviation joins the number's letters in the pool that 'About' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficient and competent are near synonyms, both describing someone who does a job well.

clue.text: From one brief look there's a label on the spear

parts.note: a tag is a small label attached to something
a lance is a long spear used by mounted soldiers

explanation.surface: A tag has been tied onto a spear, visible at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing something at a glance means taking it in with a single quick look.

clue.text: Anyone can remove chagrin

indicators.note: read as re-move, moving the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Anybody is able to get rid of disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance and chagrin are both feelings of vexation or irritation.

clue.text: Need no luxury

definitions.meaning: a basic essential, something one cannot do without

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a requirement, and also an essential item as opposed to a luxury.

clue.text: Had done some sketching although looking tired

definitions.meaning: past participle of the verb for making pictures with a pencil
a face looking pinched and haggard with fatigue is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of the verb for sketching, and also an adjective for a strained, exhausted face.

clue.text: Record radical item that's a disgrace

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
red describes a political radical
it means a thing, an item

explanation.surface: A record of a radical item turns out to be shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to disgrace them, and the noun means disgrace or loss of reputation.

clue.text: Beds Scotsman

definitions.meaning: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; also
..., short for Alexander, is a traditional nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.walkthrough: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county north of London; Sandy is a small town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy is a town in Bedfordshire and also a stock nickname for a Scottish man.

clue.text: Upscale performer

parts.note: upscale suggests upmarket, but here it means a singer whose part lies at the top of the musical scale

explanation.definitionFit: A soprano sings the highest vocal part, up the scale.

clue.text: Swindler put hands on instrument

parts.note: in card games a hand is the set of cards a player holds
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A con artist puts his hands on a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a cheat who wins at cards by trickery, a kind of swindler.

clue.text: Sorry case needs money put into it

definitions.text: Sorry case needs money put into it

parts.note: sorry can mean poor or pitiful, as in a sorry state
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A pitiful container is crying out for donations.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor box is a collection box in a church for donations to the needy.

clue.text: Convenience call?

parts.note: a public convenience is a toilet, and calling at one is a trip to the loo, while a call is also a social visit

explanation.surface: A social call made purely because it suits the caller.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a euphemism for going to the toilet, and literally means calling on someone.

clue.text: Cross river in outer limits of Valladolid

indicators.note: the river is placed between those two letters
outer limits are the first and last letters of the city's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a river on the edge of the Spanish city of Valladolid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross and vexed both mean angry or annoyed.

clue.text: Contraltos can embrace opera

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Contralto singers are able to hug an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is an opera by Puccini.

clue.text: Sweetheart's more frenzied love

indicators.note: frenzied means wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover's passion grows ever more frenzied.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, the lover in Shakespeare's play, is used for any male sweetheart or ardent wooer.

clue.text: Chief officer, accountant to leave island

indicators.note: to leave means to be taken out of the island word

parts.note: Majorca is a Spanish island in the Mediterranean
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A senior officer and his accountant are departing from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Chief' and 'officer' describe the answer: major means chief, and a major is an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means principal or chief, and is also the rank of an army officer above captain.

clue.text: Lady has fewer than a dozen to take permanent possession of

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name, a lady
ten, written as the Roman numeral X, is fewer than twelve

explanation.surface: A woman owns not quite twelve of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize it and incorporate it permanently.

clue.text: Work at prison's a crime

definitions.meaning: a job done by someone serving time, literally work on the inside
a robbery carried out with help from someone working for the victim

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a theft committed with the help of an insider, and literally a job done inside jail.

clue.text: Any dope prepared for occasion when public may visit

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Any fool can get ready for a day when visitors come.
explanation.definitionFit: An open day is when an institution such as a school admits members of the public.

clue.text: Worker on short time gets a wrong mark — it's a disease

parts.note: a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
a cross, X, is the mark a teacher puts by a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A labourer on reduced hours is marked down, and it turns out to be an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthrax is a serious bacterial infection of animals and people.
